title: U.S. House · Massachusetts's 9th District
area: Southeastern Massachusetts and Cape Cod, including New Bedford, Fall River, Plymouth, Barnstable and the islands of Martha's Vineyard and Nantucket.

context.text: Incumbent Bill Keating defeated Craig Swallow in the September 1, 2026 Democratic primary. R. Tyler MacAllister won the Republican primary unopposed.

candidates.name: Bill Keating
candidates.ballotNote: Won the September 1, 2026 Democratic primary against Craig Swallow.

summary.text: Bill Keating is the incumbent Democratic U.S. Representative for Massachusetts's 9th District. A former Massachusetts state legislator and Norfolk County district attorney, he serves on the House Armed Services and Foreign Affairs committees.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree (1974) and master's degree (1982) from Boston College and a law degree from Suffolk University (1985).
Served in the Massachusetts House of Representatives (1977-1984) and the Massachusetts State Senate (1985-1998).
Served as Norfolk County District Attorney from 1999 to 2010 before his election to the U.S. House in 2013 (having previously represented the state's 10th District beginning in 2011).

priorities.text: Supporting responsible gun-control legislation, including background checks before all gun purchases and opposing the legal availability of high-capacity, military-grade firearms.
Treating access to high-quality, affordable health care as a basic human right and building on the Affordable Care Act.
Investing in conservation and coastal restoration, including wastewater management on Cape Cod.

positions.summary: Supports background checks before all gun purchases and opposes the legal availability of high-capacity, military-grade firearms; has cosponsored bills including the Fix Gun Checks Act and the Large Capacity Ammunition Feeding Device Act.
positions.quote: He supports background checks before all gun purchases, in addition to stemming illegal possession or transfer of firearms and improving safety technologies like personalized weapons and trigger locks. Bill strongly opposes the legal availability of high-capacity, military-grade firearms, which are strictly weapons of war.

positions.summary: Describes himself as pro-choice, cites a consistent 100% rating from NARAL Pro-Choice America, and supports preserving Title X family-planning funding.
positions.quote: Bill Keating is pro-choice and proud to have consistently received a 100% rating from NARAL Pro-Choice America.

positions.summary: Says access to high-quality, affordable healthcare is a basic human right and supports building on the Affordable Care Act.
positions.quote: Bill believes that access to high-quality, affordable healthcare is a basic human right.

positions.summary: States support for raising the federal minimum wage.
positions.quote: He strongly supports raising the minimum wage to $10.10.

record.text: Assigned to the House Committee on Foreign Affairs and the House Committee on Armed Services, including the Cyber, Information Technologies and Innovation Subcommittee and the Intelligence and Special Operations Subcommittee, in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

Served as Ranking Member of the Foreign Affairs Subcommittee on Europe in the 118th Congress (2023-2024) and chaired the Foreign Affairs Subcommittee on Europe, Energy, the Environment and Cyber in the 117th Congress (2021-2022).

candidates.name: R. Tyler MacAllister
candidates.ballotNote: Won the September 1, 2026 Republican primary unopposed.

summary.text: R. Tyler MacAllister is the Republican nominee for Massachusetts's 9th District. He serves on the Mattapoisett Select Board. He had not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey and no campaign website or additional public statements were found at time of research.

background.text: Born in Massachusetts; as of 2026 served on the Mattapoisett Select Board.

sources.title: United States House of Representatives elections in Massachusetts, 2026

researchNotes: No campaign website or public statements beyond his Ballotpedia biography were found for R. Tyler MacAllister. Federal key votes and FEC finance totals for Keating are added separately by script.
